requirement: Document and protocol overview
reason: Reading guidance and headings introduce obligations in their substantive subsections.

requirement: Start a stream session with a server greeting
reason: The session accepts a connected byte stream and writes an untagged greeting before reading commands.

requirement: CRLF, ASCII command atoms, client tags and response framing
reason: Malformed commands get BAD without a state change; case-insensitive ASCII command recognition does not widen atoms to Unicode.

requirement: Independent client sequencing and response handling
reason: Client duties include unique outstanding tags, waiting for continuations, honoring sequence-number ambiguity rules, accepting unsolicited or unknown extensions, and waiting for LOGOUT completion. Server counterparts are listed separately.

requirement: Positive ascending message identities and UIDNEXT across expunge
reason: Gateway UIDs come from assigned message IDs; SELECT and STATUS do not fall back to the highest extant message after an expunge.

requirement: UIDVALIDITY when a backend replaces or restores its UID namespace
reason: Stable non-reused IDs are the gateway premise. The constant cannot signal a restore or reset that invalidates that premise; do not claim arbitrary store replacement or nonpersistent UID support.

requirement: Immutability of every representation after UID assignment
reason: Source octets surviving conversion is narrower than unchanged envelope and all reported sections for the UID across conversions, sessions and backend changes. The engine reads from its backend and does not itself enforce this invariant.

requirement: One-based sequence order and immediate renumbering on EXPUNGE
reason: Multiple removals emit sequence numbers in the current sequence space, not UIDs or the original positions.

requirement: System flags, keyword atoms and advertised persistence
reason: System flags and supported keywords round-trip through STORE, APPEND, COPY and FETCH; the gateway supplies persistence, not the protocol session alone.

requirement: Recent is session-sensitive and cannot be assigned with STORE
reason: The first eligible selecting session claims new arrivals; different sessions do not blindly share a flag, and a client cannot set the system flag.

requirement: Shared Recent claims across gateway processes or restart
reason: The watermark is process-local; evidence from two sessions sharing that state does not prove durable or multi-process claims.

requirement: Rev2 must not depend on rev1 Recent semantics
reason: There is only a rev1 baseline; it still exposes Recent and this is not rev2 mode evidence.

requirement: Internal date sources for SMTP arrival, APPEND and COPY
reason: The server dates arriving SMTP mail, APPEND preserves the specified instant, and both gateway copy paths preserve source metadata.

requirement: RFC822.SIZE counts the same octets the session returns
reason: The size matches the mode-specific converted message; this is not an equality assertion against source octets after conversion.

requirement: Envelope fields are structured and distinct from SMTP envelope addresses
reason: Parsed message headers drive ENVELOPE including absent fields, defaults and address groups.

requirement: BODY and BODYSTRUCTURE structure, recursion, counts and extension order
reason: Separate basic, text, encapsulated message and multipart forms are exercised for RFC822 MIME structure, not rev2 MESSAGE/GLOBAL.

requirement: Command availability follows authentication and mailbox selection
reason: Authenticated commands cannot run on a fresh session, selected commands require a mailbox, and BAD preserves existing state.

requirement: LOGOUT BYE then tagged OK; no implicit expunge
reason: A normal LOGOUT reports both responses before closing and preserves deleted-but-not-expunged messages.

requirement: Abortive closure after unsafe command framing or transport loss
reason: Only normal and intentional reportable closure paths are proven; a dropped stream cannot carry a final BYE.

requirement: Quoted strings, literals, parenthesized data and NIL are distinct forms
reason: Literal framing counts exact octets and server literals have no client continuation; NIL is not a quoted string or an empty list.

requirement: Unsigned sequence and UID sets, wildcard and numeric bounds
reason: Set syntax excludes zero and overflow; sequence and UID sets go through distinct resolution paths.

requirement: End-to-end 63-bit body part and message sizes
reason: A bounded STATUS=SIZE extension and size consistency on ordinary bodies do not establish rev2 large-message grammar and backend capacity.

requirement: Seven-bit text versus binary literals and transfer-encoding failures
reason: Rev1 text must not leak forbidden octets; the BINARY path has separate literal and unknown-encoding behavior, not proof of every rev2 part type.

requirement: Case-insensitive INBOX, hierarchy delimiter and rev1 mailbox name encoding
reason: The delimiter and reserved inbox name have defined handling; UTF-8 output in a rev1 session requires negotiation.

requirement: Rev2 UTF-8/NFC and OLDNAME behavior as the mode baseline
reason: NFC persistence and a negotiated extension are exercised; neither establishes default rev2 mode, compatibility switching or all OLDNAME sites.

requirement: Discover a personal namespace without listing other users
reason: The response has one slash-delimited personal namespace and NIL for the unused other-user and shared categories.

requirement: Shared or other-user namespace advertisement and enumeration
reason: The gateway exposes neither optional namespace, so obligations conditional on exposing them are not supported features.

requirement: Report new messages and changed flags when responses are legal
reason: NOOP refreshes counts and flags, unsolicited FETCH includes UID, and the ordinary idle stream does not emit updates without a command.

requirement: Keep EXPUNGE out of ambiguous commands and pending continuations
reason: Wire cases cover plain FETCH, STORE and SEARCH, incomplete literal input, and serialized saved-result dependencies.

requirement: Idle autologout timeout and BYE
reason: The default timeout is separate from the test's shortened clock; expiry sends BYE rather than purporting to complete a command.

requirement: Advertise capability tokens and complete CAPABILITY
reason: The greeting and command expose the capabilities of the rev1 session; advertisement is not proof that every advertised extension is complete.

requirement: Advertise and negotiate IMAP4rev2 including the dual-mode ENABLE switch
reason: The server advertises IMAP4rev1; unknown ENABLE tokens are ignored, and no command switches to rev2. Not an approved rev2 policy decision.

requirement: NOOP and CHECK report normally without requiring commands to modify mail
reason: CHECK is implemented as a refresh; NOOP is an any-state command.

requirement: PREAUTH and anonymous sessions
reason: The optional preauthenticated entry point and anonymous access are not offered; normal sessions must authenticate.

requirement: STARTTLS in the pre-auth state with post-TLS capability discovery
reason: The server performs the TLS transition on the existing socket, advertises the appropriate pre- and post-upgrade capabilities, and does not run pre-TLS buffered commands as authenticated input.

requirement: Deployment-wide TLS policy and active TLS downgrade detection
reason: A tested handshake is a component proof, not proof of all installed listener configurations; active downgrade detection and server identity verification also need the client.

requirement: PLAIN exchange, LOGIN, syntax/auth failure and rate limits
reason: The offered mechanism and LOGIN have framed failure responses without disclosing credentials; gateway throttling is exercised separately.

requirement: Negotiated SASL security layer and mechanism-specific service names
reason: The offered mechanism is PLAIN, which does not negotiate a SASL security layer or name an application service. TLS is separate.

requirement: Additional authentication mechanisms without plaintext credentials
reason: The engine returns NO for unsupported mechanisms such as GSSAPI. This does not satisfy the rev2 recommendation to offer additional non-plaintext mechanisms.

requirement: Tagged BAD for malformed SASL base64, not for valid encoding with wrong credentials
reason: The engine takes the same strict decoder path for initial and continuation responses. This is an engine witness, not a production compatibility decision for all rev1 or rev2 installations.

requirement: TLS-capable cleartext listener withholds plaintext authentication
reason: LOGINDISABLED and withheld AUTH=PLAIN agree with rejected credentials before TLS, and authentication becomes available after TLS. A deliberately configured TLS-less test session is a different case.

requirement: ENABLE supported extension options without changing CAPABILITY
reason: Existing extension enablement is additive, reports accepted options and does not change the token list. This is not ENABLE IMAP4rev2.

requirement: Advice to designers of future ENABLE extensions
reason: Rules for specifying future capabilities do not add an operation to this gateway.

requirement: SELECT and EXAMINE emit mailbox metadata and change selection without expunge
reason: Successful selection reports counts, flags, UIDs and mode; NO deselects, and read-only body reads do not set Seen.

requirement: CREATE, DELETE and RENAME enforce folder bounds and protect INBOX from deletion
reason: Production route persistence covers duplicate names, INBOX deletion and refused merges; the engine grammar is independently exercised.

requirement: Full hierarchical naming and special INBOX rename in the production store
reason: The fixture demonstrates the engine's special INBOX rename with a supporting backend; the production API protects standard folders including INBOX from rename.

requirement: Persistent account subscription state including absent folders
reason: The engine can delegate subscription changes, but the gateway supplies no durable subscription store. Treating existing folders as subscribed does not implement the required transitions.

requirement: LIST reference, patterns, hierarchy, attributes and extended return data
reason: The engine covers delimiter, wildcard, CHILDREN, CHILDINFO and LIST-STATUS shapes with suitable backend data. This does not override the production subscription gap.

requirement: Full rev2 LIST option policy and duplicate return options
reason: Extended rev1 parsing and selection are narrower than the full rev2 rules, including repeated options and the missing gateway subscription state.

requirement: Illustrative LIST, SEARCHRES and session transcripts
reason: Examples illustrate requirements covered by command rows and do not add server behavior.

requirement: STATUS returns requested attributes without changing selection
reason: Explicit attributes and the supported DELETED extension are tested; the command is not a new-message probe for a selected mailbox.

requirement: APPEND framing, options, destination validation and UID disclosure
reason: The server validates before continuation when possible, accepts one framed literal, and discloses UID metadata only where the backend returns usable data and rights allow it.

requirement: Atomic APPEND failure in production
reason: The import transaction rolls back on a persistence or quota failure. A generic engine backend must separately provide an atomic append.

requirement: An unconditional new message on every successful APPEND
reason: Ordinary APPEND creates a new message but the product's Sent submission-matching exception intentionally returns the recent existing copy.

requirement: Default rev2 UTF-8 message headers and full rev2 APPEND literal limits
reason: The rev1 path requires UTF8=ACCEPT for the extension; neither rev2 defaults nor all rev2 sizing are claimed.

requirement: IDLE continuation and DONE, including UID in unsolicited FETCH
reason: IDLE changes allowable responses while waiting for DONE and emits an identifying UID with flag updates.

requirement: CLOSE expunges silently in read-write mode; UNSELECT does not
reason: Read-only close and deselection preserve messages; selected read-write close removes marked messages without intermediate EXPUNGE responses.

requirement: SEARCH keys, dates, charset selection and UID result form
reason: Rev1 mode and explicit extension options are proven, including the production account's date boundary. This does not model every optional charset as supported.

requirement: Default UTF-8 and ESEARCH response without a RETURN option in rev2
reason: The advertised mode uses rev1 defaults; ESEARCH and UTF-8 extension paths do not establish different rev2 defaults.

requirement: SAVE and saved-result search variable in selected state
reason: The saved sequence/UID interpretation follows the selected mailbox and ordered commands, not a globally shared saved set.

requirement: NOTSAVED response on resource refusal
reason: No enforced saved-result resource threshold or NOTSAVED wire path exists; normal backend failure is not that response.

requirement: FETCH sections, partial octets, macros and BODY.PEEK seen semantics
reason: Sections and partial offsets operate on what the client receives; nonmutating reads do not set Seen in read-only selection.

requirement: Structured MESSAGE/GLOBAL and its nested section traversal
reason: The recursive RFC822 MIME witness does not demonstrate the rev2 MESSAGE/GLOBAL grammar and traversal.

requirement: STORE replaces, adds or removes flags; SILENT suppresses usual echo
reason: Selection-scoped flag mutation obeys the requested operation and the ordinary versus SILENT response form.

requirement: COPY and MOVE use one atomic set transfer in the gateway
reason: The PostgreSQL handler preserves the source properties and rolls back the whole set on a later failure. COPYUID pairs the source and destination identifiers; MOVE's old copies are removed.

requirement: Set-wide rollback when an arbitrary library backend lacks SetMailbox
reason: Production uses the atomic set route. The engine cannot roll back earlier writes by a backend that only offers per-message operations.

requirement: Rev2 UIDPLUS baseline and UIDNOTSTICKY for every backend
reason: Available mapping depends on backend UID metadata in the supported rev1 path; this is not universal rev2 UIDPLUS or a nonsticky-store implementation.

requirement: UID namespace selects by UID and returns required identifiers
reason: The UID command namespace has separate dispatch and a UID FETCH always carries UID; in the rev1 session sequence prefixes remain sequence numbers.

requirement: Unknown and unimplemented experimental commands get BAD
reason: The server does not pretend to implement arbitrary private X commands or advertised-by-someone-else extensions.

requirement: OK, NO and BAD carry distinct meanings and framing
reason: Success, operational failure and accepted-syntax boundaries have distinct completion forms; BAD cannot reset the selected state.

requirement: Response codes conditional on unimplemented features
reason: Do not infer UIDNOTSTICKY, NOTSAVED, optional authentication mechanisms or future ESEARCH/LIST response labels from the generic response-code grammar.

requirement: Inventory formal grammar productions and actual alternatives
reason: The existing detail indexes 148 rev1 and 232 rev2 ABNF productions plus the rev2 sequence-set incremental alternative. Inventory checks validate coverage, not that all ABNF alternatives are supported.

requirement: Conformance to complete rev2 grammar including mode transition
reason: Shared wire witnesses do not establish the complete new grammar, 63-bit sizes, default UTF-8, removal of rev1-only constructs or dual-mode negotiation.

requirement: Gateway TLS protocol floor, cipher baseline and implicit handshake
reason: The gateway's TLS config and accepted/rejected handshakes are tested; system-wide listener exposure and external installation proof are separate.

requirement: Password quality and service-wide resistance to authentication abuse
reason: These witnesses prove bounded login paths, not the whole deployment's password and throttling policy. Do not infer it from the library's backend interface.

requirement: Security of a mechanism that uses MD5
reason: No MD5-based SASL mechanism is offered. A legacy MIME Content-MD5 header is not an authentication mechanism.

requirement: Historical, IANA, bibliography and optional extension recommendations
reason: These sections address history, registries, reference dependencies and optional feature selection; active server token and command rules are listed under their defining sections. Appendix F is not the rev2 compliance baseline.
